name: New Age/Occult

objectives.text: Identify God as a living Person who knows, speaks, and loves rather than a force or energy
Recall that God forbids fortune-telling, magic spells, and asking spirits for help
Explain why Christians pray to God alone instead of trusting lucky charms, crystals, or the stars
Explain that God made the sun, moon, and stars to serve as lights and signs so they cannot rule a person's life the way horoscopes claim
Describe what Jesus meant by calling himself the light of the world and why Christians look to him rather than to an inner light for truth
Explain why Christians avoid Ouija boards, séances, and other attempts to contact the dead using the account of Saul and the medium at Endor
Summarize pantheism and contrast it with the biblical teaching that God created all things and is distinct from his creation
Compare the New Age claim that humans are divine with the serpent's promise in Eden and God's refusal to share his glory
Apply the first commandment to occult practices such as astrology, tarot, and spirit guides
Identify common New Age and occult practices in popular media and match each to the biblical warning that addresses it
Analyze how monism, the belief that all is one, erases the distinctions between God and creation and between good and evil
Contrast the doctrine of reincarnation with the biblical teaching of one life followed by judgment and bodily resurrection
Distinguish the New Age idea of a Christ consciousness from the historical, incarnate Person of Jesus Christ
Connect the ancient Gnostic claim to secret saving knowledge with similar claims in New Age spirituality and Paul's response to them
Explain from Deuteronomy 18 why God forbids divination and how he instead provides guidance through his prophets and now his completed Word
Analyze how the apostles confronted sorcery and spirit possession in Acts and what these accounts show about Christ's authority
Contrast the New Age concept of karma with the biblical doctrine of salvation by grace through faith
Evaluate the moral relativism of New Age spirituality against the biblical teaching of objective truth and God's moral law
Evaluate the Eastern mystical roots of popular meditation and yoga practices by contrasting emptying the mind with biblical meditation on God's Word
Construct a defense of the personal, triune God against impersonal views of the divine by showing how eternal love and communication require Persons
Develop a biblical account of spiritual warfare regarding the occult that rests on Christ's victory and avoids both fear and fascination
Design a respectful gospel conversation with someone who holds New Age beliefs modeled on Paul's address at Athens

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies (God as Person, forbidden divination, prayer to God alone, Jesus as light, Ouija and spirits, pantheism, humans as gods, first commandment, monism, Christ consciousness, Gnosticism, Deuteronomy 18, moral relativism, Eastern mysticism, personal God, spiritual warfare). Merged the pantheism summary and Creator and creature comparison, and reframed the 'we are all gods' item around Genesis 3. Sharpened the grade 11 defense of God's personality around the Trinity so it no longer repeats the grade 5 pantheism item. Added missing competencies: astrology and creation, identifying occult practices in media, reincarnation versus resurrection, karma versus grace, Acts encounters with sorcery, and a capstone gospel conversation. Added precise scripture and confession anchors throughout.
